evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Social cohesion and trust indicators in HDI and GPI the relational interdependence values central to East Asian collectivist well-being]

[PATH:empirical] Cross-national survey data comparing generalized trust (e.g., World Values Survey trust item) with network-based trust measures (e.g., family/community obligation scales) across East Asian and Western societies, analyzing their correlations with subjective well-being indices. — Directly tests whether the standard generalized trust indicator underestimates well-being in collectivist contexts by comparing its predictive validity against relational trust measures.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of studies on the relationship between social cohesion indicators (e.g., HDI's trust component, GPI's social capital sub-index) and well-being outcomes in East Asian versus Western populations. — Synthesizes existing evidence to assess whether systematic measurement bias occurs across cultures, providing a broader empirical foundation for the hypothesis.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical critique of the construct validity of 'generalized trust' as a universal indicator, drawing on cultural psychology frameworks (e.g., Markus & Kitayama's independent vs. interdependent self-construal) and cross-cultural measurement theory. — Clarifies the conceptual misalignment between the operationalization of trust in HDI/GPI and the relational interdependence valued in East Asian collectivism, informing whether underestimation is a measurement artifact.

qualifier.condition: when trust is operationalized as generalized trust toward strangers rather than as network-based mutual obligation

C006.object: the relational interdependence values central to East Asian collectivist well-being
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Social cohesion and trust indicators in HDI and GPI the relational interdependence values central to East Asian collectivist well-being]

[PATH:empirical] Comparative analysis of East Asian national surveys (e.g., Japanese General Social Survey, Korean General Social Survey, Chinese General Social Survey) against HDI and GPI indicators — Directly tests whether relational interdependence values (e.g., family harmony, social obligation) correlate with HDI/GPI metrics in East Asian populations, revealing gaps in coverage.

[PATH:literature] Cross-cultural validation studies of well-being scales (e.g., Singelis et al., 1995 on self-construal; Kitayama & Markus, 2000 on cultural models of happiness) — Systematic review of existing psychometric evidence can establish whether interdependence values are systematically underrepresented in composite indices like HDI and GPI.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical framework from relational cultural theory (e.g., Jordan, 2010; Miller, 2002) applied to index construction — Provides a conceptual basis to argue that HDI and GPI employ individualistic assumptions, thus failing to capture collectivist well-being dimensions; can be tested by mapping index components onto relational constructs.

C007.subject: community-level reciprocity metrics in East Asian collectivist contexts
C007.predicate: predict subjective well-being more strongly than
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: community-level reciprocity metrics in East Asian collectivist contexts standardized HDI trust indicators]

[PATH:empirical] Re-analysis of East Asian Social Survey (EASS) modules on social networks and trust (2010-2020 waves) to compute community-level reciprocity indices (e.g., gift exchange frequency, mutual aid) and compare their correlation with subjective well-being against HDI trust indicators — Directly tests the hypothesis using existing longitudinal survey data from the target region, allowing within-region comparison of metric predictive power.

[PATH:empirical] Experimental vignette studies in Japan, South Korea, and China measuring subjective well-being responses to scenarios varying reciprocity norms vs. institutional trust cues — Causal evidence can isolate the relative contribution of reciprocity metrics versus HDI trust indicators, addressing confounds in observational data.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of published studies on social capital and well-being in East Asia, coding for reciprocity-specific measures (e.g., generalized reciprocity, network-based exchange) versus standardized trust items — Synthesizes existing evidence to assess whether reciprocity metrics consistently outperform trust indicators across diverse samples and methods, identifying effect size heterogeneity.

C008.subject: East Asian collectivist values
C008.object: by HDI and GPI metrics even if augmented with community-level reciprocity metrics
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: East Asian collectivist values by HDI and GPI metrics even if augmented with community-level reciprocity metrics]

[PATH:empirical] Comparative analysis of subjective well-being surveys (e.g., World Values Survey, Gallup) across East Asian countries, focusing on items measuring collectivist values (e.g., group harmony, filial piety) and their correlation with HDI and GPI components. — Directly tests whether standard metrics capture variance in collectivist well-being; if correlations are low, supports the hypothesis.

[PATH:empirical] Ethnographic or mixed-methods studies on community-level reciprocity (e.g., gift-giving, mutual aid networks) in rural vs. urban East Asian settings, comparing these to HDI/GPI scores. — Provides ground-truth data on whether augmented reciprocity metrics align with lived experiences of well-being, potentially refuting or confirming the hypothesis.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical critique from capability approach literature (e.g., Sen, Nussbaum) applied to East Asian contexts, arguing for culturally specific dimensions of well-being. — Offers conceptual grounding for why HDI/GPI may miss collectivist values, supporting the hypothesis even if empirical data is mixed.
